newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sugar panel to discuss sugar crop prospects.
newsitem.headline: Sugar panel to discuss sugar crop prospects.

text.p: Prospects for the new sugar crop will on Wednesday be discussed by European Union sugar officials as part of preparations for the launching of the 1997/98 (July/June) export tender.
Sugar demand and supply forecasts help calculate surpluses to be exported with and without subsidies.
"Discussions are starting a bit earlier this year," said a Commission official, adding three rounds of talks were planned in the weekly EU sugar management committee.
In the last two seasons, the EU launched new export tenders in August -- one month later than usual -- and the same pattern could be continued this year.
A decision could be taken on July 2 or July 9.
The EU sugar panel is also expected on Wednesday to fix the 1997/98 (July/June) most-favoured-nation (MFN) raw cane sugar import quota of around 85,000 tonnes.
The sugar is expected to be supplied mainly by Cuba and Brazil at a reduced tariff of 98 ecus a tonne.
Subsidised sugar supplies in 1997/98 for the Canary islands, Azores, Madeira and the Aegean islands are also expected to be fixed.
